summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, and cardiomyopathy due to Chagas disease presented with fever, nausea, vomiting, and diffuse abdominal pain. He was found to have MSSA bacteremia originating from an infected left arm AV graft, which showed signs of cellulitis. Blood and wound cultures confirmed methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus. He was started on vancomycin, then transitioned to cefazolin, and underwent removal of the infected graft. A temporary dialysis catheter was placed in the right external jugular vein, later converted to a tunneled catheter. Repeat blood cultures became negative, and his clinical condition improved. He was discharged home on a four-week course of IV cefazolin administered during dialysis, with close outpatient follow-up planned with infectious disease, transplant, and primary care teams.
